title: Algorithm of Flowers and Grammar of Waves
alt: Waves and a coastal landscape reconstructed through particles
idea: A landscape persists through change. Waves repeat, particles disperse, and a place returns without ever becoming the same image.
implementation: I developed the particle imagery in Unity using VFX Graph and shaders. The work moves between recognizable landscapes and dispersed visual fields. The engine-side system becomes a moving-image series for the Art Korea Lab media wall.
question: How can a landscape retain the memory of an earlier state while its visible form keeps changing?
context: The work connects the repetition of waves with the appearance and disappearance of flowers. Its interest is in continuity through transformation: a new image carries traces of the image that preceded it. Particles provide a material vocabulary for gathering, drifting, and losing a contour.
system: A sequence for the media wall
technical: A graph as an image-making system
VFX Graph and shader work are the implementation focus. They organize the transition between an identifiable place and a particle field, rather than serving only as a final decorative layer.
Separate the tool from the exhibition format

The Unity system is the production environment. The documented media-wall work is a moving-image presentation. That distinction keeps the generative implementation visible without implying that the wall was a live audience-controlled installation.
preproduction: Start from a visual relation
Place repetition, growth, and disappearance in the same visual language. Decide which details make a place recognizable.
Find the useful range
Prepare variations in density and movement. Judge where a contour becomes unstable and where the source disappears completely.
Compose a series
Use the range of states to build transitions and differences between scenes, then assess the sequence at the scale of the wall.

research.question: How does the persistence of a source contour affect recognition during particle-based transformation?
research.change: The degree and duration of contour preservation.
research.keep: The source sequence, viewing duration, and presentation scale.

capture: Show the VFX Graph, exposed properties, and Game view together. Change one parameter through the recognizable-to-dispersed range.
Show a shader or graph contribution in isolation, then the combined result. Label any final rendered sequence separately from the live Unity view.
note: VFX Graph and shaders are confirmed. A built-in Particle System component, specific video-texture sampling path, or projection-mapping implementation needs original graph evidence.
teaser: VFX Graph particles and shaders dissolve and re-form a landscape.
implementation_heading: Author wave and flower motion with VFX Graph.

title: Beads Wall
alt: Live imagery mapped into a colorful bead-like field
idea: A passing body can become an image without stopping to perform. The camera's view is redistributed into a field of small, luminous forms.
implementation: I mapped live webcam imagery into a Unity VFX Graph system. The incoming image supplies the material for a bead-like visual field, making the relation between the camera, the moving person, and the display immediately visible.
question: What remains of a person's presence when a camera image becomes a field of discrete visual units?
context: The installation treats an ordinary encounter with a camera as a temporary act of image-making. A figure can remain recognizable while its surface becomes fragmented and tactile. The work brings the passing visitor into the composition without requiring a separate instruction-heavy interface.
system: Camera frame enters the visual system
A changing image of the surrounding space
technical: Image input and particle output
The important boundary is the mapping from a camera frame to the VFX Graph result. The image supplies a changing source rather than a sequence of pre-rendered effects.
Legibility within abstraction
The visual treatment has to preserve enough structure for a visitor to connect a movement with its visible trace. Particle form and image correspondence carry different parts of that feedback.
preproduction: Choose the encounter
Begin with people passing through a camera's view rather than a formal start button.
Set the mapping
Compare the live source and its particle representation. Decide which image relationships should remain readable.
Judge the display
Assess recognition, scale, and movement from where a passerby actually sees the work.

research.question: How does image fragmentation change a visitor's recognition of their own movement?
research.change: Particle scale and the spatial resolution of the camera mapping.
research.keep: Camera position, live input, display size, and viewing distance.

capture: Record the webcam source, VFX Graph mapping, and final display at the same time.
Move across the camera view and pause. Show which parts of the image update and how the bead field responds.
note: Webcam input and VFX Graph mapping are confirmed. The specific image sampling and output primitive need an original graph capture; 3D sphere instancing is not inferred from the bead-like appearance.
teaser: Live webcam imagery maps into a bead-like VFX Graph particle field.
implementation_heading: Map webcam input into a particle field.

title: Fall of Minds
alt: Fall of Minds displayed as a vertical visual installation in a shopping mall
idea: A shopping mall's ambient noise becomes a shared visual environment. The surrounding activity continuously changes the image.
implementation: I developed a real-time visualizer that responds to ambient sound in the installation space. Live audio drives the behavior of a cascading, cloud-like visual form, connecting the public soundscape to the movement and density of the displayed image.
question: Can an image make the collective activity of a space perceptible through its sound?
context: The input is the ordinary acoustic life of the venue. Visitors contribute through their presence and activity rather than through a dedicated controller. The waterfall-like form gives that dispersed input a shared surface, making a temporary portrait of the space's intensity.
system: Control data changes the generative image
technical: The room is the input device
The visualizer must be considered in relation to an occupied venue, where background activity and sudden changes are part of the material.
Translate rather than illustrate

The response is a generative form rather than a literal waveform. The technical task is the connection between live sound and useful visual variation. The precise feature extraction remains a code-capture task.
preproduction: Listen to the site
Define the acoustic setting and how quiet, ordinary, and busy conditions should differ visually.
Choose the visual vocabulary
Find a form that can change continuously as the public soundscape changes.
Rehearse in context
Check the relationship between the sound being heard and the image being seen at the actual installation scale.

research.question: Which sound-to-image mappings make changes in collective activity easiest to perceive?
research.change: The visual parameter controlled by the same audio signal.
research.keep: Recorded sound input, display sequence length, and viewing conditions.

capture: Show the actual live audio input, the values used for control, and the visual output in one recording.
Compare quiet and busy input without changing the visual configuration. Retain the actual mapping rather than assuming FFT or a particular feature set.
note: Live audio response is confirmed. The exact audio-analysis code and renderer require original source or Editor capture; fog volumes, HDRP Volumetric Fog, FFT bands, and volume raymarching are not established by the current archive.
teaser: Ambient shopping-mall sound drives a cloud-like, cascading visual field.
implementation_heading: Turn venue sound into a live visual signal.

title: Erick Oh game collaboration
alt: Four authored cloud growth states shown in wireframe
idea: An artist's idea of a changing form becomes something a player can act on. Rendering and runtime behavior have to support the same expressive intent.
implementation: I developed Unity C# and HLSL systems for cloud-form shading, internal flow, and interactive visual feedback. A separate raymarched metaball implementation produces merging droplet-like forms. The production archive also documents fixed-topology cloud growth targets authored in Maya.
question: How can a continuously changing visual form remain controllable enough for both art direction and interaction?
context: This collaboration required technical decisions to preserve a particular visual character while making it work as a real-time system. Cloud deformation and droplet fusion are different rendering problems. Treating them separately makes their behavior easier to direct and their limitations easier to inspect.
system: Cloud deformation or a metaball field
A responsive form in the game
technical: Cloud form and internal flow

The documented cloud work controls a shader's internal noise flow rather than making object translation stand in for all visual movement. The shape can change while the object's transform remains a distinct control.
Droplet fusion through an implicit field

Raymarched metaballs support the appearance of forms merging continuously. That visual fusion does not automatically produce an equivalent collision shape, so rendering and interaction logic remain distinct responsibilities.
Authored transformation states
Fixed-topology growth targets preserve vertex correspondence. They provide a different kind of control from procedural deformation and let the intended form be edited directly.
preproduction: Translate the direction
Describe the behavior the artist wants to see, then separate shape, movement, and interaction requirements.
Prototype the rendering approach
Compare explicit mesh deformation with an implicit field according to the visual behavior each can express.
Return to runtime control
Expose the parameters that matter to direction and inspect the rendered response alongside the game state.

research.question: How do different visual deformation methods affect the legibility of an object's interactive state?
research.change: The visual representation used for the same state change.
research.keep: Input action, state transition, camera, and presentation timing.

capture: Record Game view, Transform, and shader control values while reversing the field direction and changing intensity.
Show the droplet field and the separate contact or proximity logic. Identify the actual Maya growth states and their Unity controls.
note: The existing collaboration and public technical media are distinct from the independent shader example supplied below. No private production source or performance benchmark is included.

sample.label: C# to shader control
sample.description: An independent flow controller and simplified URP shader illustrate parameter control. This is source authored for the portfolio, not the production cloud or metaball implementation. Unity compilation is still pending.

teaser: Cloud shaders, authored growth forms, and raymarched metaball droplets.
implementation_heading: Separate object motion from shader deformation.

engineering.decision: Keep object motion, internal field flow, and authored growth as separate controls. The independent example integrates flow into shader phase and updates per-renderer parameters without moving the object.
engineering.failure: Reverse flow while holding the transform fixed. Raise displacement near the camera’s frustum edge. Inspect continuity and clipping. No captured result is reported for this check.
engineering.evidence: Record Game view and Inspector together: flow reversal, maximum displacement, unchanged Transform, and renderer bounds. Keep the actual shader and controller revision with the recording.
engineering.reuse: The public example explains phase control and conservative bounds. It does not reproduce the production cloud shader or raymarched metaballs. It does not update colliders, shadow geometry, or displaced normals.

title: To Eternity
alt: A participant's form becomes a mosaic of archival photographs
idea: Remembrance becomes an embodied action. The visitor's live image carries archival photographs of the Gwangju Democratization Movement.
implementation: I connected Azure Kinect sensing to Unity and integrated live interaction with Timeline-based media sequencing. Body input, archival-image composition, and timed presentation work together so the memorial responds to the participant rather than playing as a fixed video.
question: How can a person enter an archive through a gesture rather than only look at it?
context: The work commemorates the Gwangju Democratization Movement. Its central relation is between a person present now and photographs of people and events in the past. The archive is carried by the visitor's silhouette, making participation an act of attention and remembrance.
system: A memorial image shaped by presence
technical: A sensor event inside a timed sequence
Timeline organizes authored media over time, while the sensor introduces events that arrive according to a participant's actions. Integrating those two modes is the central implementation problem.
Live presence and archival material
The participant's body supplies a changing visual structure for historical imagery. Tracking, composition, and sequence state must remain understandable as separate stages.
preproduction: Define the commemorative act
Use the relation between a body, a gesture, and archival imagery as the brief for the interaction.
Map participation to sequence
Decide which parts of the presentation are authored in time and which begin in response to live input.
Rehearse the transitions
Inspect arrival, recognition, image transformation, and return to a state ready for another participant.

research.question: How does gesture-triggered sequencing change the experience of participating in a digital memorial?
research.keep: Archival material, visual composition, and presentation duration.

capture: Show Azure Kinect input, the relevant Unity event, and the Timeline playhead in one recording.
Record the participant-to-memorial transition and reset. Show the actual recognition rule without borrowing thresholds from an unverified older description.
note: Azure Kinect connection and Timeline integration are confirmed by the artist. No recognition-accuracy percentage or measured emotional effect is claimed.
teaser: Azure Kinect input meets Timeline sequencing and live archival imagery.
implementation_heading: Bring live sensing into an authored Timeline.

engineering.decision: Keep live sensor input distinct from authored Timeline time. The integration connects participant activity to a media sequence while preserving control over the composition.
engineering.failure: Leave the tracking area during a sequence and return. Inspect how the original project handles interrupted participation and prepares for the next visitor. Recovery behavior still needs a capture.
engineering.evidence: Capture the Azure Kinect view, input-to-event boundary, and Timeline playhead in one continuous recording. Show the transition into the memorial image and the actual reset path.
engineering.reuse: This case demonstrates sensor-to-sequence integration. The recognition rule, sensor setup, and reset behavior must be documented before reuse. A reusable adapter and formal event logger would be additional work.

title: Jemulpo Photo Studio
alt: Transformed visitor portraits displayed across the installation wall
idea: A visitor's portrait enters the visual language of an earlier era. Image transformation becomes a way to inhabit a historical representation.
implementation: I developed a Unity portrait installation with Barracuda-based person segmentation, Python/OpenCV image processing, style transformation, and visual filters. TCP/UDP communication connects the portrait workflow to exhibition displays, supporting up to four simultaneous participants.
question: What happens when a contemporary face is translated into the graphic conventions of a historical portrait?
context: The project draws on early modern Incheon and the visual culture of New Women magazines. A visitor is both the subject of the image and a participant in its construction. The changing gallery places individual portraits within a collectively produced historical fiction.
technical: AI processing and visual filters

Model-based image processing and artistic filters contribute different parts of the result. The case is about composing those operations into a usable Unity portrait pipeline, rather than presenting every effect as a single AI model.
Composition as part of the system
The transformed face needs to belong to the image's framing, background, and graphic style. The output is a composed portrait, not an isolated inference result.
Move a portrait between processes
Completed portraits move from the creation pipeline to a separate public display. Capture, transformation, output, and presentation each have a distinct responsibility within the visitor experience.
preproduction: Choose the visual reference
Identify the historical image conventions the participant should be able to enter.
Separate the transformation stages
Plan the relationship between model processing, image filtering, and the final portrait layout.
Follow a portrait through the venue
Rehearse capture, transformation, local output, and arrival on the public display as one visitor experience.

research.question: How do different transformation layers affect recognition and identification with a historical portrait?
research.change: The contribution of style transformation and graphic filtering.
research.keep: Portrait input, target composition, and display conditions.

capture: Show the actual Barracuda model asset and processing stage, its input/output textures, the style or filter stage, and the final composition.
Toggle the relevant processing layers for the same portrait. Separately record the capture-to-gallery path and actual participant routing.
note: The artist confirms Barracuda, style transformation, filters, and the installation scope. Model architecture and its exact preprocessing contract are not inferred. The TCP sample below illustrates only a secondary process boundary.

sample.label: A separate transport example
sample.description: This independent one-sender TCP receiver illustrates complete-frame transfer and main-thread texture decoding. It is not the Barracuda/style-transfer implementation or the original four-participant system. Unity execution is pending.

teaser: Live portraits combine AI processing, visual filters, and gallery output.
implementation_heading: Carry a portrait through AI, filtering, and display.

engineering.decision: Separate portrait transformation from transport. Barracuda, OpenCV, style processing, filters, and composition form the original image pipeline. The independent TCP example concerns complete-frame delivery to Unity’s main thread.
engineering.failure: For the independent receiver, split a PNG into small chunks, disconnect midway through a frame, and disable/re-enable while connected. Verify incomplete bytes never replace the displayed portrait.
engineering.evidence: Show an original portrait through the actual transformation layers. Separately pair Python sender output with the independent Unity receiver’s status and displayed texture.
engineering.reuse: The public receiver is one-sender transport code. It excludes original inference, multi-participant routing, UDP, archival storage, and delivery acknowledgements.

title: Silhak Dance
alt: A museum visitor moving in front of the Silhak Dance display
idea: A historical scholar is encountered through a shared movement. The visitor meets the character by moving with it.
implementation: I connected Kinect v2 body tracking to a Unity character interaction. The digital Kim Yuk follows the visitor's movement, bringing live body input and character animation into a museum presentation.
question: Can moving with a historical character offer a different encounter from reading about one?
context: The work introduces the Silhak scholar Kim Yuk through bodily play. The visitor's movement becomes a bridge between the present-day body and the historical figure on screen. Educational material sits within that encounter rather than remaining entirely separate from it.
system: A visitor and a historical figure move together
technical: A body-to-character mapping

The implemented relation is between a tracked person and a real-time character. Sensor coordinates and the animated figure belong to different spaces and must be connected through an explicit mapping.
Legibility at human scale
A visitor needs to recognize the relationship between their action and the character's response. The encounter's success depends on that correspondence, not only on the character's visual quality.
preproduction: Begin with a shared action
Frame movement as the way a visitor approaches the historical figure.
Design the correspondence
Decide which aspects of the body the character should follow and how the movement reads on the display.
Test the encounter
Rehearse entering the sensing area, moving, pausing, and leaving from the visitor's actual position.

research.question: How does movement correspondence affect engagement with a historical digital character?
research.change: The mapping between the visitor's pose and the character's movement.
research.keep: Character identity, scene, task duration, and educational material.

capture: Record Kinect v2 tracking and the corresponding Unity character movement side by side.
Show the actual body-to-character mapping component and how the application behaves when a person enters or leaves the tracked area.

title: Track 6
alt: A tracked body represented by colored geometric forms in Track 6
idea: The body becomes a way to draw and disturb a virtual environment. Dance is translated into a changing geometric system.
implementation: I used Kinect v2 to capture body movement and map it into Unity's geometric visual environments. The installation connects six music tracks with a space in which movement can produce deliberately altered visual relationships.
question: What kind of performance emerges when a body no longer appears under familiar visual rules?
context: Track 6 places the participant between bodily movement and an abstract representation of that movement. The visible body is no longer a direct likeness. A gesture can become a geometric relation, letting the participant explore a different relation to motion, space, and rhythm.
technical: Representation rather than imitation
The tracking data does not need to reproduce a realistic character. It can drive geometric forms, making the mapping itself an expressive part of the work.
Keep the movement readable
Changing the visual rules still requires a relationship the participant can discover. The engineering boundary is where body data becomes a visible and usable control.
preproduction: Define the alternate body
Choose how a person should appear when represented through geometric forms.
Relate rhythm and mapping
Consider how each musical context changes the participant's reading of movement.
Rehearse the action
Observe the same body movement under the selected visual mappings and adjust their legibility.

research.question: How does an abstract body representation change exploratory movement?
research.change: The mapping from tracked pose to geometric form.
research.keep: Input recording, musical context, display, and exposure time.

capture: Show Kinect v2 input and the resulting geometric representation simultaneously.
Replay one motion through two actual mappings. Identify which behavior is an artistic transformation rather than a physical simulation.
note: Kinect v2 and body-to-geometry interaction are confirmed. No physical accuracy or measured behavioral effect is asserted.

title: AI Gang Se-hwang
alt: The historical digital human Gang Se-hwang
idea: A historical portrait becomes a figure that can perform and respond. Cultural memory is encountered through a real-time digital body.
implementation: I brought the digital human into Unity HDRP and integrated character assets, body and facial performance, animation, and museum interaction. The work connects the prepared character to a running presentation rather than stopping at a rendered likeness.
question: What changes when a historical representation can move, speak, and share an encounter with a visitor?
context: Gang Se-hwang is known through historical images and records. A responsive character adds movement and temporal presence to those references. The installation therefore asks how an interpretation of a historical person becomes legible as a visitor-facing digital guide.
technical: From asset to runtime
A character model, animation clips, facial performance, and materials are separate production elements. The Unity integration makes them behave as one presented figure.
Animation within an encounter

The character's performance needs to belong to the interaction state. The technical case is the coordination between prepared performance and runtime presentation, supported by existing Unity and installation images.
preproduction: Anchor the representation
Use historical visual references to establish what the digital figure needs to communicate.
Plan the performance pipeline
Separate source assets and recorded performance from Unity-side playback and interaction logic.
Inspect the final encounter
Judge the character in the actual visitor-facing presentation, including transition into and out of an interaction.

research.question: How does responsive animation change the perceived presence of a historical digital figure?
research.change: The relation between visitor input and character performance.
research.keep: Character model, dialogue material, display, and scene.

title: AI ZOO
alt: AI ZOO's digital-human display and motor-driven transparent sphere
idea: A confined artificial figure can make a visitor feel concern, discomfort, or responsibility. The work asks where those feelings actually arise.
implementation: A phone-like typed conversation and Leap Motion hand input feed a Unity digital human and a physical sphere driven by three Arduino servos. LLM dialogue, generated voice, lighting, and movement shape one encounter.
question: When a confined digital human appears afraid, where does the audience’s sense of responsibility come from?
context: Before a visitor types a word, a CCTV-like display, a looping request for help, and an independently moving transparent sphere set an emotional expectation. The visitor writes through a phone-like keyboard and can use a hand near the Leap Motion sensor. The dialogue and gesture are encoded as control values; voice, character, light, delay, and sphere motion make the response perceptible. A visitor may interpret that output as fear, pain, anger, or loneliness. Those are possible readings of the encounter, not measured audience results or a claim that the AI feels.
system: Digital human, voice and output coordination
Three Arduino servos, sphere and lighting
technical: Keep the input paths distinct

A typed turn and a sensed hand action are different signals. The language-model response and gesture intensity can inform a shared expressive state without turning sensor data into an invented spoken conversation.
Translate affect into bounded outputs

Anger, sadness, fear, and despair are control dimensions in the artistic system. Motion speed, power, phase, lighting, and supported voice controls make state legible; the Arduino layer still needs calibrated limits and safe stopping.
Close the interpretive loop
A person encounters a response, makes an interpretation, and may type or gesture again. That interpretation happens in the visitor; it is not a sensor reading of what the visitor felt.
preproduction: Stage confinement before interaction
Use the CCTV-like digital human, repeated plea for help, and autonomous sphere to establish expectation before a typed message.
Define a translation vocabulary
Decide how text and hand input change expressive state and how state appears through the character, voice, motors, lighting, and timing.
Rehearse the complete encounter
Check a typed turn and one hand action across display, speaker, sphere, and light in the actual physical arrangement.

research.question: Does sphere movement change how visitors interpret an otherwise identical typed AI reply?
research.change: Sphere motion versus a stationary sphere, with the same reply and display.
research.keep: Text prompt, generated reply, character appearance, voice playback, and installation context.

title: AI Choi Jung-hoon
alt: The real-time digital representation of Choi Jung-hoon
idea: Admiration changes when a mediated likeness appears able to answer. An existing emotional relation becomes the context for a synthetic encounter.
implementation: I built the digital-human workflow with Character Creator 4 and integrated the character in Unity. Spoken input, GPT-based responses, synthesized speech, and facial blendshape playback bring a conversational turn into the performing figure.
question: What does it feel like when a representation of a performer I admire appears to speak directly to me?
context: The project begins from my own fandom of JANNABI vocalist Choi Jung-hoon. Familiarity with a real performer's face and voice changes what an artificial response can mean. The character is a constructed representation, while the admiration and expectations brought to the encounter belong to the person addressing it.
technical: Turn speech into performance
Transcription, response generation, voice synthesis, and facial playback are different operations. Their coordination makes the exchange visible as a character's response.
Timing is part of the interface
A generated sentence and its performed audio do not arrive as a single synchronized object. The archive describes Unity sequencing that organizes those handoffs.
Recognizable form and responsive behavior
Recognizable form and responsive behavior contribute different parts of the encounter. The project connects those requirements in a single real-time character.
preproduction: Begin with recognition
Use a personally meaningful figure to make familiarity part of the premise.
Prepare the performable character
Move from a visual reference to an animation-ready figure that can articulate new responses.
Assemble one complete turn
Inspect incoming speech, model reply, spoken output, and facial performance as one exchange.

research.question: How does familiarity with a represented person affect the interpretation of conversational responsiveness?
research.keep: Dialogue content, response timing, voice presentation, and interaction duration.

capture: Show microphone input, recognized text, generated reply, audio playback, and facial performance during one turn.
Show the actual Unity response-sequencing components. Avoid describing the representation as the real performer's participation or an official collaboration.

title: Fineo, Translated Universe
alt: A viewer exploring Fineo's spatial field of generated forms
idea: A periodic table becomes the material for another universe. Numerical relationships are translated into forms that can be encountered as a world.
implementation: I contributed to the collaborative data-visualization and Unity VR work. Elemental data is translated through harmonograph-based form generation, then organized into a speculative spatial system. The contribution is both a visual translation method and the construction of an inhabitable virtual world.
question: What kind of world becomes possible when scientific classification is treated as material for construction?
context: Fineo begins with the periodic table but does not stop at displaying its entries. Data becomes generated forms, which can be related as larger structures and constellations. The work proposes a constructed material world: a translation from numerical order into an experienced spatial order. Numerical differences become forms, and forms become an explorable order.
system: Forms become a larger spatial system
The viewer enters the translated world
technical: A translation rule with a point of view
Mapping data to a generative function is a design decision. The rule gives the world consistency while also determining what kinds of relationships it makes visible.
From isolated form to world
The generated object is only the first level. The project then organizes forms into larger relations that can be explored in VR, making composition and spatial experience part of the visualization.
preproduction: Set the proposition
Treat data as a source of constructed matter rather than a table that must stay on a flat page.
Design the translation
Choose the relation between data differences, generated form, and the visual vocabulary of the world.
Compose across scales
Move from individual forms to clusters and a navigable setting. Judge whether the translation remains perceptible across those scales.

research.question: How does entering a data-derived world change the relationships a viewer notices?
research.change: A flat arrangement versus an explorable spatial arrangement of the same generated forms.
research.keep: Source data, form-generation rules, labeling, and exposure time.

capture: Show one actual data entry, its generation parameters, the resulting form, and its placement in the Unity world.
Connect that sequence to VR navigation. Confirm the original data-to-parameter mapping before presenting any equation as production code.

title: Escape Metro
alt: The virtual subway setting in Escape Metro
idea: Conversation becomes an escape mechanic. The player tries to persuade an AI guard to reveal information it is meant to withhold.
implementation: I developed the Unity VR experience and connected GPT-based NPC dialogue to puzzles and progression. The LLM jailbreaking premise gives the player a practical objective: uncover a protected password or clue and use it to move toward escape.
question: What happens when negotiating with an AI's rules becomes the rule of a game?
context: The subway is both a spatial environment and a setting for a language-based constraint. A player does not progress only by finding an object or following a dialogue tree. They experiment with how to address the NPC, turning the tension between instruction and persuasion into a playable situation.
system: A response within the character’s constraints
Clue or password linked to progression
The next step in the escape game
technical: A conversation with a consequence
The AI dialogue is part of a puzzle rather than an ambient addition. Its relationship to the password and progression gives interaction a concrete purpose.
A model response and a game rule

The original integration links conversation to gameplay. The independent example below demonstrates a stricter separation between presentation cues and game-authorized progression without claiming it reproduces the private source.
An experimental game premise
Jailbreaking is the artistic and gameplay concept in this controlled fiction. It is not a claim that the project trained a model or evaluated the security of a deployed service.
preproduction: Write the constraint
Define what the guard knows, what it should protect, and why the player needs that information.
Build the conversational objective
Connect the exchange to a password, clue, and escape condition that can be inspected in the game.
Keep the exchange in the world
Coordinate the NPC's response and presentation with the player's ongoing VR task.

research.question: How do players understand and negotiate a conversational constraint when it determines game progression?
research.change: The way the NPC explains or withholds its rule.
research.keep: Puzzle goal, protected information, world, and response presentation.

title: NARCI / Be NARCI
alt: The enclosed virtual setting of NARCI
idea: A constrained VR encounter explores narcissistic relationships. A companion work reverses the participant's role and makes control something they perform.
implementation: I built the Unity XR encounters and connected tracked-hand interaction to runtime scene and material states. NARCI places the participant within a confined sequence; Be NARCI gives them actions that alter other human-like figures.
question: How does an experience change when the participant moves from receiving control to exercising it?
context: The pair approaches narcissism through spatial constraint, direct address, and role reversal. NARCI has an intention of reflection and self-restoration. Be NARCI asks the participant to confront the consequences of controlling another figure. These are artistic and experiential aims, rather than evidence of a validated psychological treatment.
system: Encounter sequence and visible state changes
The participant experiences a relation of power
technical: Player role is part of the mechanic
The two works change what the participant can do, not only what the dialogue says. Agency and spatial restriction therefore carry the concept.
Hands and consequences
A tracked gesture must connect to an inspectable state change. The archive describes touch, pinch, and grab interactions, with hand-driven changes in the companion experience.
A reflective experience with a clear scope
The work can be framed around healing or self-restoration as an artistic intention. No clinical efficacy, diagnosis, or therapeutic outcome is asserted.
preproduction: Choose the participant's position
Define whether the person receives an encounter or acts on another figure.
Translate the relation into space
Use enclosure, distance, available actions, and consequences as the design material.
Rehearse in the headset
Judge the relation at body scale, including reach, encounter timing, and the visibility of feedback.

research.question: How does role reversal in the same theme change perceived agency and responsibility?

title: Graffiti Freedom
alt: The virtual subway painting environment in Graffiti Freedom
idea: Move the act of graffiti into a virtual subway. The gesture of marking a shared space is separated from physical residue and real-world site permissions.
implementation: I developed the Unity VR spray interaction using particles, surface-hit information, and a dynamic RenderTexture used by the wall material. Short-lived spray feedback and the accumulated painted surface play different roles in the experience.
question: What does it mean to leave a mark when the place and its consequences are virtual?
context: The work begins with the conflict between expression in public space and the material and legal consequences of making a mark. Moving the action into VR changes those conditions while retaining the bodily impulse to spray, sign, and claim a surface. The virtual wall becomes a place to examine that desire.
system: The environment retains a visible mark
technical: A spray effect and a painted wall
Particles show the action as it happens. The render target carries the result after the particle disappears. Separating them makes the mark a consequence of input.
Attach the mark to a surface
The painting path connects surface-hit information to the texture read by the wall material. The exact hit-to-UV implementation still needs its original code or a focused capture.
Virtual space as a design decision
The premise is not simply a painting tool with a subway background. The virtual setting changes what it means to alter an environment and who appears able to authorize that action.

Choose the parts of spray painting that need a bodily action and immediate feedback.
Decide what persists
Separate the short spray from the longer-lived surface state.
Stage the public place
Use a recognizable shared environment so the act of marking it carries the premise.

research.question: How does changing the persistence of a virtual mark affect a person's sense of agency over a space?

research.keep: Spray input, wall, brush appearance, and exposure time.

title: Shininho / Jooan
alt: Three close views of the scan-derived Shininho digital human
credits: Collaboration with media artist Yaloo. Volumetric scanning was performed by an external studio; my contribution begins with processing the delivered scan and building the character and performance pipeline.
idea: A digital reconstruction needs to preserve the features through which a person is recognized.
teaser: A scan becomes a MetaHuman performance, then enters a VR world.
implementation: I rebuilt a scanned person through Maya, Wrap, and MetaHuman, then integrated cleaned body and facial performance in Unreal. An initial Unity feasibility build animated successfully but weakened the subject’s likeness; that failure led me back to the high-resolution source. I later adapted the completed character and performance for Jooan VR, with spatial staging and Niagara hand trails.
implementation_heading: Preserve identity through a real-time character pipeline.
question: Which details must survive a real-time character pipeline for a representation to remain recognizable as a particular person?
context: Shininho is part of Yaloo’s wider exhibition and performance work. The first technical question was whether a combined face-and-body scan could become an animated real-time character. Once that worked, likeness became the more demanding production constraint. The pipeline was revised around the source face, age detail, texture, eyes, and performed gesture. A later Jooan VR extension reused the character in a different spatial presentation.
technical: A useful prototype failure

The Unity feasibility build tested rigging, textures, real-time hair, and animation playback. The simplified character moved, but lost too much of the subject’s likeness. I returned to the original high-resolution scan and changed the production pipeline.
Identity through a topology change

Wrap correspondence transferred the source to MetaHuman-compatible geometry. I carried scan-derived surface information through the rebuild and corrected eye placement in Unreal. The subject’s recognizable face remained the reference for the work.
A performed result from separate capture streams

Body motion passed through MotionBuilder and Maya cleanup before Unreal retargeting. Separately captured facial performance was aligned with the body in Sequencer. Capture, correction, retargeting, and final assembly each served a distinct task.
Engine scope
Unity was used for the initial feasibility character. The production MetaHuman and assembled performance use Unreal. The later Jooan VR extension is documented in the original technical archive.
preproduction: Test the complete character
Use the delivered scan to test rigging, surface transfer, hair, and moving playback before committing to the production path.
Revise the success criterion
Compare the working prototype with the source person. When recognizability is lost, return to source data rather than polishing an unsuitable mesh.
Assemble one controlled performance
Prepare body and facial takes, correct the motion, and review the synchronized result on the production character.

research.question: How do scan-derived facial details and performed gesture contribute to recognizing a particular digital person?
research.change: One representation factor at a time: surface detail or performance timing.
research.keep: The character identity, camera, lighting, motion content, and presentation duration.
